poC_plan: Week 0: Provision 2x A100 reserved nodes in dedicated pool; baseline load test with 50tps sustained
Week 1: Run synthetic and replay tests; measure p50/p95/p99 for streaming vs non-streaming
Week 2: Add KV/prefix caching, test cold vs warm cache impact on p99
Week 3: Canary traffic from 5% of production; validate routing fallback and quantized variant behavior
Deliverable: SLO measurement report + recommended reserved GPU commitment (monthly)
measurement_definition: Client-side vs server-side: want both. Client will emit client-send/client-receive timestamps; server will emit ingress/egress timestamps and per-stage timers.
p50/p95/p99 computed on end-to-end latency (client_receive - client_send) for product SLA, and on server-egress for operational SLA.
Streaming: define per-token latency and first-byte latency separately. SLO targets differ: first-byte p95 < 120ms, per-token p95 < 20ms for hot KV hits.
Non-streaming (batch gen): measure total completion time; p95 target < 250ms for short prompts (<128 tokens).
Clock sync: require client clocks to be NTP-synced; we'll use request-id to correlate traces when clocks diverge.
Sampling: collect 100% traces for 1 hour per day during the POC, then 1% continuous in steady-state; store raw for 30 days for audit.
Percentiles computed over sliding 1-hour windows for alerting; monthly SLA computed from daily aggregates excluding scheduled maintenance windows.
sla_negotiation_items: Definition: Agree on canonical metric (end-to-end vs server-egress) to use for billing credits and SLA credits
Exclusions: maintenance windows, force majeure, customer-side network incidents; define clear RCA steps
Remediation: SLA credit tiers for p95 and p99 breaches; propose 10% credit for p99>target more than 3 days in month
Data residency: must guarantee EU model routing for EU-origin requests; audit logs available for 90 days
Measurement transparency: shared dashboard with raw histograms + exportable CSV for legal review
capacity_requirements: Target steady-state: 1200 concurrent sessions, average 30 tokens/sec per session during peak, spike up to 4000 concurrent for 3-5 minutes
Model mix: 60% medium (7B) local variants, 30% large (33B) for high-quality recommendations, 10% rerankers (2B).
GPU planning ask: reserve 12x A100-equivalent GPUs with headroom for burst to 18 GPUs; prefer predictable placement to avoid inter-tenant noisy neighbors
Throughput guarantee request: sustained tokens/sec guarantee with per-minute throttling policy to avoid token storms
client_concerns: How to align product-facing SLA (end-to-end) with ops-facing server metrics — they want both but only one in contract
Streaming measurement is fuzzy: browser vs mobile differences; need standard header definitions
Cache warm-up: big effect on p99 — want guidance on warmup windows and priming strategies
Cost: want to compare reserved cost vs burstable on-demand during holiday spikes
